newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Army controls key installations in Islamabad.
newsitem.headline: Army controls key installations in Islamabad.

text.p: Pakistani army units took over key installations in Islamabad on Tuesday after President Farooq Leghari dissolved parliament and dismissed Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, the official news agency APP said.

It said troops in battle gear had entered the capital at about 2 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday) and taken over the state-run radio and television stations, the telecommunications company, cabinet offices and the prime minister's secretariat.

Witnesses said troops were on guard at the television and radio stations and on one road leading to Bhutto's residence, but there was no sign of any major military deployment or any restriction on movement of traffic in the capital.
Bhutto's spokesman Farhatullah Babar told Reuters by telephone earlier that Bhutto was at her official residence in Islamabad, but was not taking calls.
Asked if there had been any military deployment, he said: "No, no such thing."
Bhutto has been in power since general elections in October 1993. The president has constitutional powers to dismiss elected governments and dissolve parliament's lower house.
